decision.rationale: Accepted diagnosis for execution cf997605885642759ee33920e2c9e2ef: terminal reach passes (terminal error 0.007642608585867386 m below the 0.01 m reach tolerance; reach_passed true), while the sampled settling check fails - the 6 selected holding-window rows at 0.30-0.35 s span position error 0.007642608585867386-0.05813810428573256 m against the 0.01 m limit and tip speed 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s against the 0.02 m/s limit (holding_position_passed false, holding_speed_passed false), with terminal tip speed 0.6351726092425104 m/s. The retained recipe sets both editable tip-speed terms to zero (holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0, terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0) while tip_speed_scale_m_s is 0.02, so normalized squared world tip speed carries no cost at the scheduled holding nodes or at the terminal node. Concrete hypothesis: with zero tip-speed cost the optimizer has no incentive to shed tip speed before or during the holding window, so a bounded positive tip-speed cost will lower holding-window and terminal tip speed while preserving the reach solution. This is one bounded candidate: terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0 -> 0.01 as the single terminal scaled squared-speed term, and holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0 -> 0.1 as the integration-step-weighted sum at the scheduled holding nodes (a larger per-second value is selected because each holding node contributes in proportion to the integration step, whereas the terminal term is one node). Scale, scheduling and all other recipe fields are unchanged; no raw scalar objectives are compared across weights. Expected effects stated separately: holding speed should fall from the recorded 0.635-1.581 m/s band toward the 0.02 m/s limit and holding position error toward 0.01 m if the speed excess is overshoot-driven; terminal reach error should remain below the 0.01 m tolerance; computation may show a different iteration/stopping profile (baseline mean_update_s 17.263 s, 35 deadline misses, stopping counts Solve_Succeeded 1 / User_Requested_Stop 34), noting wall-clock misses are computation signals that do not inject simulated delay. Possible adverse effects: a tip-speed penalty can trade against position and push terminal error past the tolerance that currently passes with limited margin, can enlarge holding position error, and can add iterations and wall time on a run already far above the 0.01 s control period. Observations that would weaken the hypothesis: holding-window speed remaining in the 0.635-1.581 m/s band while reach degrades, terminal speed unchanged with terminal error rising, or more unusable/nonconverged updates without speed change - then tip-speed cost is not the settling limiter and attention belongs on solver stopping and plan quality. Known coverage limits (6 selected rows only; earlier sampled motion and warm-plan/iteration traces not read/not retained; no counterfactual replay) mean this execution can support or weaken, not prove, the hypothesis; absence of causal proof does not prohibit this bounded test. local_comparison is omitted: the read allowance for this phase is zero and no legal saved baseline update with effective horizon 0.01 s is established from retained evidence, and inconclusive screening does not prohibit the complete experiment.

decision.rationale: Bounded two-weight experiment, adopted because the diagnosed dominant supported observation is a speed failure and the two exposed tip-speed penalties are both at legacy zero. Baseline cf997605885642759ee33920e2c9e2ef reaches (reach_passed true, terminal_error_m 0.0076426 m below the 0.01 m tolerance) but fails to hold (holding_position_passed, holding_speed_passed, joint_reach_holding_passed all false); across all 6 recorded final-window samples (0.30-0.35 s) sampled speed spans 0.6352-1.5810 m/s against the 0.02 m/s limit and sampled error spans 0.0076426-0.0581381 m against the 0.01 m limit, with terminal_speed_m_s 0.6352 m/s and late_max_speed_m_s 1.5810 m/s. The recipe currently records terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0 and holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0, so the legacy plan carries no explicit tip-speed objective. Hypothesis: enabling a modest positive weight on squared normalized tip speed at the plan terminal node (terminal_tip_speed_weight) and on nodes at/after the configured settling-window start (holding_tip_speed_weight) makes the optimizer favour plans that decelerate the tip before and within the holding window, lowering sampled holding speed while keeping reach. Why these weights: they are the only exposed knobs and they encode exactly the failed quantity (tip speed); the tip both enters the window already moving (terminal speed 0.6352 m/s) and moves within it (up to 1.5810 m/s), so a single weight would leave one regime uncosted. Scale (tip_speed_scale_m_s 0.02) and scheduling are left unchanged: the terminal term remains a single scaled squared-speed term and the holding term remains an integration-step-weighted node sum. Expected effects: (reach) should stay passing given the 0.0076426 m margin, though a terminal speed/position trade-off could erode it; (holding position) indirect improvement if the tip settles, reducing the 0.0581381 m peak; (holding speed) primary target, expected below the 0.635-1.581 m/s range toward the 0.02 m/s limit; (computation) the holding term is a cheap node-weighted sum so cost is expected roughly unchanged, but the run already averaged 17.263319 s per update against a 0.01 s period with 35/35 deadline misses and only 6 noninitialization updates applied, so overrun may dominate the closed-loop outcome and the trial may be inconclusive rather than decisive. Values kept modestly positive and equal (0.01 each) because raw weight magnitude does not establish cost-term importance without retained cost contributions, and normalized squared tip speeds at these speeds are already O(1e3). Possible adverse effects: a weight that dominates the objective could command aggressive braking or overshoot, degrade reach above the 0.01 m tolerance, or change solver usability/update count. Observations that would weaken the hypothesis: a re-run still showing holding-window speeds far above 0.02 m/s with terminal speed still near 0.635 m/s; again only ~6 applied updates, indicating overrun masks the weight; terminal_error exceeding 0.01 m; or no measurable difference between the two weights because few holding nodes are scheduled. No dominant cause and no winning value is presumed; this is a bounded, reversible trial and a single execution cannot establish causality.

decision.rationale: Accepted diagnosis (possible, bounded): the failing sampled criterion includes holding-window tip speed — across all six recorded rows of the 0.30–0.35 s window every sampled tip speed exceeds the 0.02 m/s limit (0.635–1.581 m/s), while the smallest sampled position error (0.00764 m) is inside the 0.01 m limit and the largest (0.05814 m) is not; terminal reach passes at 0.0076 m against the 0.01 m tolerance. The saved recipe shows holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0, so the holding window currently carries no tip-speed cost at all. Hypothesis: the settling failure includes residual tip speed inside the settling window, and adding a nonzero per-second squared spatial tip-speed cost at nodes at/after the window start makes the optimizer prefer settling-window trajectories that are slower at the tip, which is directly the criterion that fails. Weight relevance: holding_tip_speed_weight is defined on exactly those nodes, and explicit settling settings are present (settling window 0.05 s with position limit 0.01 m and speed limit 0.02 m/s), satisfying the parameter's requirement. I select the holding weight alone rather than also changing terminal_tip_speed_weight: terminal reach already passes, the terminal instant lies inside the penalized holding window anyway, and changing both at once would confound the one model-selected complete experiment the grant allows.
